dedupe_keys.name: wastemap waste methane assessment platform global map of solid waste methane emissions with city and site decision support tools

description: WasteMAP is a free web platform that maps methane emissions from municipal solid waste around the world and helps cities and site operators plan how to cut them. It was built by RMI and the Clean Air Task Force with funding from the Global Methane Hub. The map combines reported inventories with modelled and observed data, including EDGAR emissions, the World Bank's What a Waste database, Climate TRACE facility estimates, and satellite detections of landfill plumes from Carbon Mapper and SRON. A city decision support tool, based on a Python version of the SWEET waste emissions model whose code is on GitHub, compares collection, diversion and landfill management options, and a site tool focuses on individual landfills. The platform is free to use, and the underlying datasets are available from their original providers under their own terms. Caveats: emissions for most cities and sites are modelled, not measured, satellite plumes capture only large sources, and the platform itself states no single licence. Coverage is global. Simulation uses: landfill emission baselines and mitigation scenarios in waste capacity and climate planning. Related records: the World Bank What a Waste database (data-what-a-waste-global-database) is one of its main inputs.
